name: ha--aircon-comfort-fan-boost
description: Fan-speed boost for the 3 real climate units (LivingR climate.hol_2, BedroomB climate.v357_spalniag_2, BedroomS climate.v537_spalniam_2): when |error| (effective - target) crosses a configurable per-room threshold (default 1.0C) in either direction while the comfort program is active, fan_mode is forced to the room's boost speed regardless of current hvac/fan_only phase, with hysteresis (0.5C release margin) so it does not flap. Symmetric for summer overshoot and winter undershoot. Reuses the existing input_number.<prefix>_return_boost_fan_mode helper as the shared speed target for both this new error-threshold trigger and the pre-existing away-return trigger. A restart-safe input_boolean.<prefix>_fan_boost_active latch drives the new trigger's hysteresis. Includes a season-indicator dashboard card.

changes: apply_fan_speed_boost.js: creates 9 helpers (per room: input_number.<prefix>_fan_boost_threshold default 1.0C, input_number.<prefix>_fan_boost_release_margin default 0.5C, input_boolean.<prefix>_fan_boost_active) via input_number/input_boolean create WS commands, name field deliberately chosen so HA's auto-slugify produces the intended entity id. Patches all 3 comfort-band automations live via /api/config/automation/config/{id}: extends the existing cooling_fan_mode template var to also trigger off the new latch (OR'd with the pre-existing return_boost_active), converts the 4 hardcoded fan_mode literals (night air-clean=5, daytime no-motion=5, daytime motion-restore=3, winter heat=3) into boost-aware templates via boostAwareLiteral(), and inserts a new 'Track fan-speed boost latch (error threshold trigger)' action (mirrors the existing 'Track away transition' action) that turns the latch on when |error| >= threshold and off when |error| < threshold - margin.

add_season_indicator_card.js: idempotent (find-or-update via a '### Comfort Program Season' content marker) markdown card inserted into the my-dash AirCon lovelace view, showing winter/summer per the existing month-based climate_mode definition (Dec/Jan/Feb = winter) plus live fan_boost_active state for all 3 rooms.

backport_fan_speed_boost_terraform.js: one-off anchor-based text-transform script (not meant to be re-run) that mirrors the live patch into main.tf's 3 comfort-band homeassistant_automation resource bodies. Reuses boostAwareLiteral from apply_fan_speed_boost.js; reimplements extendCoolingFanMode/the latch-action builder as HCL-safe variants because main.tf stores multi-line Jinja templates as one physical HCL line with literal 2-char '\n' sequences, not real newline bytes, so the live-JSON-oriented functions would silently no-op against it.

main.tf: patched in place for test_aircon_livingr_room_sensor_comfort_band, test_aircon_bedroomb_room_sensor_comfort_band, test_aircon_bedrooms_room_sensor_comfort_band. BedroomS (hand-authored, not on the shared sync_climate_setup_templates.js generator) patched standalone with equivalent hand-duplicated logic rather than migrated onto the generator, per Ticket 02's resolution. No new Terraform resources or import.tf changes needed - helpers are not Terraform-tracked in this repo (confirmed zero pre-existing homeassistant_input_number/input_boolean resources).

fix_fan_boost_hysteresis_guard.js: post-ship adversarial-review fix. The latch's OFF condition (error|abs) < (threshold - release_margin) is unsatisfiable whenever release_margin >= threshold (both helpers' input_number ranges permit this), which would leave the latch permanently on with no self-release path. Adds a fan_boost_effective_margin = min(release_margin, threshold - 0.01) clamp so the release band is always at least 0.01C wide, never empty. Applied live (all 3 automations) via a targeted value_template string replace, and mirrored into main.tf (functional fix + a scoped terraform-fmt alignment fix for the 6 new "condition" keys inside the 3 latch actions, windowed to just those blocks so it does not touch the file's large pre-existing unrelated fmt drift).

checks: C1: all 9 helpers created live via input_number/list and input_boolean/list (create, not update - none pre-existed), entity ids match the intended <prefix>_fan_boost_threshold / _fan_boost_release_margin / _fan_boost_active slugs
C2: all 3 automations patched and re-enabled (automation.test_aircon_{livingr,bedroomb,bedrooms}_room_sensor_comfort_band state=on) after /api/services/automation/reload

C3: ON-condition template rendered True at error=1.5 (summer overshoot >= threshold) and error=-1.5 (winter undershoot, |error|>=threshold), True at exactly error=1.0 (>=), False at error=0.9 (below threshold)

C4: RELEASE-condition template rendered False at error=0.6 (above threshold-margin=0.5, should not release), True at error=0.4 and error=-0.4 (below threshold-margin, should release) - confirms hysteresis window (0.5-1.0C) behaves as intended, not a single flap-prone threshold

C5: cooling_fan_mode template returned normal speed (2) with latch off and no return-boost, and boosted speed (5, the return_boost_fan_mode value) under both latch-on and return_boost_active-on cases - confirms the two triggers share one output value via plain OR as decided in Ticket 01

C5b (post-review fix): RELEASE-cond with an explicit margin>=threshold configuration (threshold=1.0/margin=1.5 and threshold=0.5/margin=0.5, both otherwise permitted by the helpers' own min/max ranges) rendered True at error just inside the clamped 0.01C band and False just outside it - confirms fan_boost_effective_margin makes release reachable (band is narrow but never empty) instead of the pre-fix behavior where it was mathematically unsatisfiable and the latch would have stayed on forever until a manual input_boolean.turn_off

C6: real-world confirmation post-deploy - live template query on actual HA state (not synthetic) returned season=summer, fan_boost_active: LivingR=False BedroomB=True BedroomS=False, proving BedroomB's boost genuinely latched on during a real hot period in production, not just in synthetic template tests
C7: season-indicator card inserted into my-dash AirCon view (idempotent - re-run would update in place via content marker, confirmed find-or-update logic, not append-duplicate)

C8: main.tf backport structurally sound - quote-aware brace/bracket/paren balance check shows zero delta ({: 1274/1274, [: 457/457, (: 178/178) after the 204-insertion/99-deletion patch; new 'Track fan-speed boost latch (error threshold trigger)' alias appears exactly 3 times (once per room) confirmed via terraform fmt -check -diff output at lines 606, 994, 3872

C9: an orthogonal adversarial review subagent found the initial backport DID introduce 6 new terraform-fmt misalignments of its own (the "condition" key inside the 3 new latch actions' if/else.if blocks, 2 per room), contradicting this eval's original claim - fixed via fix_fan_boost_hysteresis_guard.js's windowed alignment pass, scoped to just those 6 lines so the file's large pre-existing, unrelated fmt drift is left untouched; re-ran terraform fmt -check -diff afterward and confirmed zero diff lines remain around any of the 3 "Track fan-speed boost latch" blocks

incidents.what: Latch's OFF condition `(error|abs) < (fan_boost_threshold - fan_boost_release_margin)` is unsatisfiable whenever release_margin >= threshold, since abs() is never negative. Both input_number helpers' live-created min/max ranges (threshold 0.5-3, release_margin 0.1-1.5) permit this configuration. If a user ever set it this way, input_boolean.<prefix>_fan_boost_active would latch on and never self-release - a silent one-way switch requiring manual input_boolean.turn_off, with no warning anywhere in the UI or code.
incidents.detected_by: Adversarial review subagent, launched per standing user request to refute the implementation against >=10 criteria before considering it done. validate_fan_speed_boost.js's original hysteresis tests only ever exercised the default 1.0/0.5 threshold/margin pair read live, never a user-adjusted or pathological combination.
incidents.fix: fix_fan_boost_hysteresis_guard.js adds `fan_boost_effective_margin = [fan_boost_release_margin, fan_boost_threshold - 0.01] | min` and uses it in place of the raw release_margin, guaranteeing the release band is always at least 0.01C wide (never empty). Applied live to all 3 automations via a targeted value_template replace, mirrored into main.tf, and validate_fan_speed_boost.js extended with explicit-literal test cases proving release is reachable (though narrow) even at threshold=0.5/margin=0.5 and threshold=1.0/margin=1.5.
incidents.root_cause: The two new input_number helpers' ranges were chosen independently (each looked reasonable in isolation against existing precedent) without checking the cross-helper invariant (margin < threshold) the hysteresis formula silently depended on.

incidents.what: The same backport script that patched main.tf introduced 6 new terraform-fmt misalignments of its own (the "condition" key inside the 3 new latch actions' if/else.if blocks not padded to align with the adjacent "value_template" key) - eval 006 originally (incorrectly) claimed the backport introduced no new formatting issues.
incidents.detected_by: Same adversarial review subagent - isolated each patched resource block and ran terraform fmt on it standalone to distinguish new drift from the file's large pre-existing drift.
incidents.fix: fix_fan_boost_hysteresis_guard.js's fixMainTf() applies a regex-based alignment fix windowed to just the 3 "Track fan-speed boost latch" action blocks (6 lines total), leaving the rest of the file's pre-existing, unrelated fmt drift untouched. Re-ran terraform fmt -check -diff afterward and confirmed zero diff lines remain around any of the 3 patched blocks.

notes: Follows the wayfinder map 'Aircon Comfort Fan Boost' (.scratch/aircon-comfort-fan-boost/): Ticket 01 (effective fan-mode composition - plain OR of the two triggers, shared return_boost_fan_mode speed) and Ticket 02 (BedroomS patched standalone rather than migrated onto the shared generator, to avoid regression risk to LivingR/BedroomB) resolved via grilling, then implemented and shipped live plus backported to Terraform in one run per explicit user override of the skill's default one-ticket-per-session pacing. terraform validate/plan was not run (provider not initialized in this environment, out of scope to init here); soundness was instead verified via structural balance checks and a manual diff-hunk read around every insertion site. An orthogonal adversarial review subagent (13 criteria) ran after shipping and found 2 real bugs (both fixed, see C5b/C9 and fix_fan_boost_hysteresis_guard.js) plus one accepted architectural limitation: the new latch action's condition templates re-derive the full per-room setup prefix (sensor reads, staleness checks, target/effective/error math) via extractSetupPrefix() rather than reading one shared effective_fan_mode variable as Ticket 01's resolution phrased it - this mirrors how every other condition/action template in these automations already works (HA does not share Jinja variables across separate template fields), so it's the same class of duplicate-setup drift risk sync_climate_setup_templates.js's other templates already carry, not a new one; a deeper fix would mean teaching that generator about the latch action, which carries the same regression risk to the 2 live rooms already on it that Ticket 02 explicitly avoided for BedroomS - left as a known limitation rather than expanded scope. terraform fmt -check -diff still reports a large diff across the rest of the file; that reflects pre-existing whitespace/alignment inconsistency present before this change (confirmed by inspecting hunks for unrelated automations) - not something introduced by, or in scope to fix as part of, this feature.
